detection.source: Google Cloud Logging Cloud Run request and structured application logs
detection.signal: Count of failed authentication callbacks and HTTP 401 responses

investigationSteps: Compare source IP, user-agent and error-class clusters with the normal five-minute baseline.
Correlate request and trace identifiers with WorkOS status and recent identity configuration changes.
containmentSteps: Apply the existing authentication rate-limit or edge block to confirmed abusive sources.
Revoke affected sessions and rotate identity credentials only when compromise evidence supports it.
runbook.escalationPath: Identity security on-call -> platform SRE on-call -> incident commander for confirmed account compromise

automatic: Open one deduplicated incident per source and error-class cluster.
Attach only allowlisted request, trace, service and revision fields to the incident.
manual: Validate provider health before blocking traffic.
Review affected accounts and invoke the account-compromise playbook when takeover is plausible.

steps: Exclude approved authentication tests and provider outage windows using change records.
Record the confirmed-positive ratio by source and tune only after identity-security approval.

testMethod.procedure: Replay 20 sanitized auth.callback_failed entries sharing one synthetic source within five minutes in an isolated alert test project.
testMethod.expectedSignal: Exactly one high-severity incident is created for the synthetic cluster and no production identity is affected.

detection.source: Google Cloud Logging Cloud Run request logs

investigationSteps: Inspect the denied route distribution and source fingerprint without copying request bodies.
Correlate the denial burst with rate-limit events, release changes and approved penetration tests.
containmentSteps: Temporarily throttle a confirmed abusive source through the approved edge control.
Preserve request and trace identifiers for authorization review.
runbook.escalationPath: Identity security on-call -> route owner -> incident commander if protected data access succeeded

automatic: Dedupe by source and route for the five-minute window.
Create a medium-severity investigation record containing the denial counts.
manual: Classify user error, scanner, policy regression or hostile enumeration.
Escalate any accompanying successful protected response for incident handling.

falsePositiveReview.cadence: Weekly and after every threshold change
steps: Compare alerts with support reports and approved security test windows.
Review noisy routes separately before changing the shared threshold.

testMethod.procedure: Send ten isolated authenticated requests that are expected to return 403 from one synthetic source during five minutes.
testMethod.expectedSignal: The grouped denial count reaches ten and creates one medium-severity test incident.

detection.source: Google Cloud Logging AlloyDB PostgreSQL logs
detection.query: resource.type="alloydb.googleapis.com/Instance" AND (textPayload=~"violates row-level security policy" OR jsonPayload.message=~"violates row-level security policy")

investigationSteps: Map the RLS violation to the database role, application revision and request trace without exposing SQL parameters.
Verify tenant context propagation and check whether any adjacent request returned cross-tenant data.
containmentSteps: Disable the affected route or revision when tenant isolation may be bypassed.
Revoke the implicated session and preserve database plus application evidence.
runbook.escalationPath: Identity security on-call -> database security owner -> incident commander and privacy lead

automatic: Open a high-severity incident keyed by database role, instance and revision.
Preserve the bounded log references and affected policy name.
manual: Reproduce the denial in staging with two synthetic tenants.
Treat any successful cross-tenant read or write as a privacy incident.

steps: Identify migration, policy-test and approved RLS verification traffic.
Require database-security approval before suppressing a policy or role combination.

testMethod.procedure: Run three denied cross-tenant fixture operations under the runtime role in isolated staging and capture the RLS log entries.
testMethod.expectedSignal: One high-severity test incident identifies the synthetic role and policy while all fixture data remains denied.

detection.query: SELECT "actorId", "targetId", COUNT(*) AS change_count FROM "AuditLog" WHERE "action" = 'admin.user.access_update' AND "createdAt" >= NOW() - INTERVAL '10 minutes' GROUP BY "actorId", "targetId" HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1

investigationSteps: Verify the actor, target, reason and approved change record for each access update.
Compare the AuditLog row with its AdminAction pair and the resulting profile role.
containmentSteps: Revert an unauthorized role change through the approved administration flow.
Revoke actor sessions and freeze privileged mutations when administrator compromise is suspected.
runbook.escalationPath: Administration security on-call -> independent administrator -> incident commander

automatic: Create one immutable review item for every privilege-change record.
Link the matching AuditLog and AdminAction identifiers without copying sensitive metadata.
manual: Obtain independent approval for the change.
Investigate and reverse any unexplained privilege grant immediately.

steps: Reconcile events against approved change tickets.
Review service or test accounts separately; never suppress human administrator grants globally.

testMethod.procedure: Create one rolled-back synthetic admin.user.access_update AuditLog fixture and execute the catalog query in isolated PostgreSQL.
testMethod.expectedSignal: The query returns the synthetic actor and target once and the test incident is high severity.

detection.source: Google Cloud Logging structured application logs
detection.signal: Server-denied attempt to remove or disable the final active organization owner

investigationSteps: Confirm the tenant, actor and attempted owner transition from allowlisted identifiers.
Verify that the server denied the change and that at least one active owner still exists.
containmentSteps: Suspend further owner mutations for the affected tenant through the approved emergency control.
Revoke the actor session when the attempt is unexplained or malicious.
runbook.escalationPath: Administration security on-call -> tenant account owner -> incident commander

automatic: Open a critical incident for every final-owner denial signal.
Dedupe repeat attempts by tenant and actor for five minutes while retaining the count.
manual: Contact a verified existing owner through an independent channel.
Review all recent membership and owner changes before restoring mutation access.

steps: Check for approved ownership-transfer rehearsals or support-led recovery.
Keep the threshold at one; refine only actor or test-environment exclusions with approval.

testMethod.procedure: Attempt to remove the sole owner of a synthetic staging organization and verify the request is denied with the catalog signal.
testMethod.expectedSignal: One critical test incident is produced while the synthetic owner remains active.

detection.query: SELECT "actorId", COUNT(*) AS export_count FROM "AuditLog" WHERE "action" IN ('user.export', 'admin.export.create') AND "createdAt" >= NOW() - INTERVAL '60 minutes' GROUP BY "actorId" HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
detection.signal: Per-actor count of user and administrator export events

investigationSteps: Review actor, target and export-type counts without retrieving export contents.
Compare the burst with approved privacy requests, administrator work and account compromise signals.
containmentSteps: Pause export capability for the affected actor through the approved emergency control.
Revoke sessions and invalidate generated artifacts when abuse is confirmed.
runbook.escalationPath: Abuse security on-call -> privacy lead -> incident commander

automatic: Open one high-severity incident per actor once five exports are recorded.
Attach event identifiers and aggregate counts, not exported data.
manual: Validate the business or privacy basis for every export.
Assess notification obligations if unauthorized data left the service boundary.

steps: Reconcile approved bulk privacy operations and support cases.
Maintain separate baselines for system, administrator and self-service actors.

testMethod.procedure: Insert five rolled-back synthetic export AuditLog rows for one actor in isolated PostgreSQL and execute the query.
testMethod.expectedSignal: The actor appears once with export_count five and a high-severity test incident is created.

detection.query: SELECT "senderId", COUNT(*) AS message_count FROM "Message" WHERE "createdAt" >= NOW() - INTERVAL '10 minutes' GROUP BY "senderId" HAVING COUNT(*) >= 100
detection.signal: Per-sender count of newly created messages

investigationSteps: Compare sender volume, recipient fan-out and reports without reading message bodies by default.
Check account age, recent session changes and automation indicators.
containmentSteps: Apply the existing message rate limit or temporarily disable sending for confirmed abuse.
Preserve message identifiers and moderation evidence under restricted access.
runbook.escalationPath: Abuse security on-call -> trust and safety owner -> incident commander for coordinated abuse

automatic: Create one deduplicated sender-volume incident per ten-minute window.
Attach sender identifier, count and recipient fan-out only.
manual: Determine legitimate high-volume conversation versus spam or compromised account.
Notify trust and safety before content inspection or user restriction.

steps: Review verified support, moderation and test-account traffic separately.
Compare alert volume with confirmed spam outcomes before tuning.

testMethod.procedure: Create 100 rolled-back synthetic Message rows for one fixture sender inside ten minutes and execute the query.
testMethod.expectedSignal: The fixture sender is returned once at count 100 and no message body enters alert evidence.

detection.query: SELECT "profileId", COUNT(*) AS listing_count FROM "Listing" WHERE "createdAt" >= NOW() - INTERVAL '60 minutes' GROUP BY "profileId" HAVING COUNT(*) >= 10
detection.signal: Per-profile count of newly created marketplace listings

investigationSteps: Review listing count, moderation status and duplicate identifiers without publishing pending content.
Compare the profile history with approved bulk listing activity and fraud indicators.
containmentSteps: Hold new listings in moderation for the affected profile.
Suspend listing creation when fraud or account compromise is confirmed.
runbook.escalationPath: Abuse security on-call -> marketplace moderation owner -> incident commander for systemic fraud

automatic: Open one profile-volume incident and attach listing identifiers plus moderation states.
Dedupe alerts by profile for the hourly window.
manual: Review welfare, legal and fraud signals before publication.
Contact the verified profile owner when compromise is suspected.

steps: Identify approved breeder or administrator bulk operations.
Tune by verified profile class only after moderation review.

testMethod.procedure: Create ten rolled-back synthetic Listing rows for one fixture profile within an hour and execute the query.
testMethod.expectedSignal: The fixture profile is returned once with listing_count ten and a medium-severity test incident.

detection.query: SELECT "userId", SUM(COALESCE("promptTokens", 0) + COALESCE("completionTokens", 0)) AS token_count FROM "AgentRun" WHERE "createdAt" >= NOW() - INTERVAL '60 minutes' GROUP BY "userId" HAVING SUM(COALESCE("promptTokens", 0) + COALESCE("completionTokens", 0)) >= 250000
detection.signal: Per-user hourly AI token volume used as the configured cost-exposure proxy

investigationSteps: Review token totals, agent type and run counts without copying prompts or outputs.
Compare the spike with approved experiments, provider pricing changes and account compromise indicators.
containmentSteps: Disable AI features for the affected actor through the approved emergency control when abuse is likely.
Apply provider-side budget or quota controls after owner approval.
runbook.escalationPath: AI platform on-call -> billing owner -> incident commander for credential compromise or runaway spend

automatic: Create one high-severity hourly cost-proxy incident per user.
Attach token aggregate, run count and agent types without prompt content.
manual: Convert tokens to provider cost using the reviewed price table.
Confirm legitimate usage before restricting a customer or rotating provider credentials.

falsePositiveReview.cadence: Weekly and whenever model pricing changes
steps: Separate approved load tests and administrator experiments from customer usage.
Recalculate the threshold against current model prices and observed baselines.

testMethod.procedure: Create rolled-back synthetic AgentRun token rows totalling 250000 for one fixture user within an hour and execute the query.
testMethod.expectedSignal: The fixture user is returned once at the threshold without exposing inputJson or outputJson.

detection.source: Google Cloud Logging Cloud Run request and structured application logs
detection.query: resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND httpRequest.status=401 AND (httpRequest.requestUrl:"/api/webhooks/stripe" OR httpRequest.requestUrl:"/api/webhooks/lago" OR httpRequest.requestUrl:"/api/livekit/webhook")
detection.signal: HTTP 401 responses from signature-authenticated webhook routes

investigationSteps: Identify provider route, source network and failure timing without recording signature headers or payload bodies.
Compare failures with secret rotation, provider delivery status and recent deployments.
containmentSteps: Rate-limit or block a confirmed hostile source without bypassing signature verification.
Rotate the affected webhook secret only through the approved secret-management procedure.
runbook.escalationPath: Platform SRE on-call -> billing or LiveKit owner -> incident commander

automatic: Dedupe by provider route and source for five minutes.
Open a high-severity incident containing counts and safe request metadata only.
manual: Verify provider health and delivery configuration.
Inspect for replay, leaked secret or misconfigured rotation before changing controls.

falsePositiveReview.cadence: After every alert and after secret rotations
steps: Reconcile failures with provider test tools and planned rotations.
Keep route-specific baselines so one provider cannot suppress another provider's alert.

testMethod.procedure: Send five isolated webhook requests with deliberately invalid synthetic signatures to a staging endpoint during five minutes.
testMethod.expectedSignal: All requests remain 401 and one high-severity route-specific test incident is created.

detection.source: PostgreSQL SignupOutbox, UsageOutbox, WebhookEvent and Notification
detection.query: SELECT queue_name, COUNT(*) AS dead_letter_count FROM (SELECT 'SignupOutbox' AS queue_name, "createdAt" FROM "SignupOutbox" WHERE "status" = 'dead_letter' UNION ALL SELECT 'UsageOutbox', "createdAt" FROM "UsageOutbox" WHERE "status" = 'failed' UNION ALL SELECT 'WebhookEvent', "createdAt" FROM "WebhookEvent" WHERE "status" = 'failed' UNION ALL SELECT 'Notification', "createdAt" FROM "Notification" WHERE "deliveryStatus" = 'failed') failures WHERE "createdAt" >= NOW() - INTERVAL '15 minutes' GROUP BY queue_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
detection.signal: Per-queue count of terminal delivery failures

investigationSteps: Identify the queue, first failure time, retry count and safe error classification.
Check downstream health, worker leases and recent schema or credential changes.
containmentSteps: Pause unsafe retries while preserving idempotency keys and failed rows.
Restore the dependency or worker, then replay only approved bounded batches.
runbook.escalationPath: Platform SRE on-call -> owning service -> incident commander for cross-queue failure

automatic: Open one incident per failing queue and fifteen-minute window.
Attach aggregate counts, oldest timestamp and safe error classifications.
manual: Determine poison message, dependency outage or worker regression.
Approve replay only after idempotency and downstream capacity checks.

steps: Separate deliberate failure drills and quarantined poison fixtures.
Review each queue baseline independently before changing thresholds.

testMethod.procedure: Create five rolled-back terminal-failure fixtures for one queue within fifteen minutes and execute the union query.
testMethod.expectedSignal: Only the fixture queue is returned at count five and no replay is performed.

detection.query: SELECT "id", "uploaderId", "storageBucket", "storagePath", "scanCompletedAt" FROM "MediaAsset" WHERE "scanStatus" = 'infected' AND COALESCE("scanCompletedAt", "updatedAt") >= NOW() - INTERVAL '5 minutes'
detection.signal: MediaAsset row transitions to scanStatus infected

investigationSteps: Confirm scanner result, media identifier, object coordinates and uploader without opening the object on a workstation.
Review related uploads, hashes and delivery attempts for spread or scanner error.
containmentSteps: Quarantine or delete the object through the approved malware flow while retaining evidence hashes.
Suspend related processing and signed delivery until the scope is understood.
runbook.escalationPath: Media security on-call -> platform SRE on-call -> incident commander

automatic: Open a critical incident for every newly infected MediaAsset.
Attach media ID, uploader ID, bucket, path and scanner timestamp without object contents.
manual: Validate the scan using the isolated malware procedure.
Review uploader activity and notify affected owners under the incident plan.

falsePositiveReview.cadence: For every detection and monthly scanner review
steps: Record scanner engine, definition version and secondary analysis outcome.
Allowlist a hash only with media-security approval and expiry.

testMethod.procedure: Upload the EICAR test fixture to isolated staging and verify the MediaAsset becomes infected without public delivery.
testMethod.expectedSignal: One critical test incident is created and the fixture cannot be downloaded through normal delivery.

detection.source: Google Cloud Logging AlloyDB PostgreSQL logs
detection.query: resource.type="alloydb.googleapis.com/Instance" AND (textPayload:"password authentication failed" OR jsonPayload.message:"password authentication failed")

investigationSteps: Identify database role, source host and instance without recording passwords or connection strings.
Compare failures with deployments, credential rotations and network policy changes.
containmentSteps: Block an unauthorized source at the network boundary.
Rotate the implicated database credential and redeploy approved consumers when leakage is plausible.
runbook.escalationPath: Platform SRE on-call -> database security owner -> incident commander

automatic: Dedupe failures by role, source and instance for five minutes.
Create a high-severity incident containing only safe connection metadata and counts.
manual: Differentiate stale deployment credentials from brute force.
Verify successful connections and privilege use after the failed attempts.

falsePositiveReview.cadence: After every alert and credential rotation
steps: Reconcile deployment and rotation windows.
Track stale consumer identities separately instead of suppressing authentication failures globally.

testMethod.procedure: Make five failed connections with an isolated synthetic role and invalid credential against staging during five minutes.
testMethod.expectedSignal: No connection succeeds and one high-severity test incident identifies the synthetic role and source.

detection.source: Google Cloud Audit Logs for Cloud Storage IAM
detection.signal: Storage IAM policy change granting a public principal

investigationSteps: Identify the bucket, actor, policy delta and affected object classes from audit metadata.
Check public access prevention, uniform bucket-level access and recent object reads.
containmentSteps: Remove public principals and enforce public access prevention through the approved infrastructure path.
Revoke exposed signed access and freeze deletion while evidence is preserved.
runbook.escalationPath: Media security on-call -> cloud platform owner -> incident commander and privacy lead

automatic: Open a critical incident for every public-principal IAM change.
Capture the bucket, actor and policy-change audit reference.
manual: Confirm whether any private object was publicly readable.
Assess exposure scope and notification obligations before closing.

steps: Verify whether the bucket is explicitly classified public; private buckets have no threshold exemption.
Reconcile the change with an approved infrastructure review and rollback record.

testMethod.procedure: Replay a sanitized SetIamPolicy audit fixture containing allUsers in an isolated monitoring test project without changing a real bucket.
testMethod.expectedSignal: One critical test incident identifies the fixture bucket and actor while no storage policy is modified.

alerts.title: Secrets detected in logs or builds

detection.signal: Count of open repository secret-scanning alerts including build or log artifacts committed to the repository

investigationSteps: Identify secret type, repository location and exposure duration without copying the secret value.
Check CI logs, artifacts and provider audit history for use of the exposed credential.
containmentSteps: Revoke or rotate the credential before removing repository references.
Invalidate affected artifacts and restrict access to logs or builds containing the secret.
runbook.escalationPath: Supply-chain security on-call -> credential owner -> incident commander

automatic: Open a critical incident for every newly open secret-scanning alert.
Attach the alert number, secret type and redacted location only.
manual: Rotate the credential and verify dependent services.
Purge or restrict retained logs and artifacts according to provider capabilities.

steps: Use provider validation and credential-owner confirmation without exposing the detected value.
Document test-token or invalid-token resolutions with expiry and reviewer identity.

testMethod.procedure: Commit a provider-approved inert test token on a disposable protected branch and confirm Secret Scanning opens then resolves the alert.
testMethod.expectedSignal: One critical test incident references the provider alert number and contains no token value.

detection.query: SELECT "actorId", COUNT(*) AS action_count FROM "AuditLog" WHERE "actorType" = 'admin' AND "createdAt" >= NOW() - INTERVAL '15 minutes' AND (EXTRACT(HOUR FROM "createdAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < 6 OR EXTRACT(HOUR FROM "createdAt" AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= 22) GROUP BY "actorId" HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1
detection.signal: Administrator actions during the configured Sydney off-hours window

investigationSteps: Review actor, action, target, reason and timing against the approved support roster.
Correlate with session changes, source access logs and recent privilege changes.
containmentSteps: Revoke administrator sessions and freeze privileged mutations when access is unexplained.
Require independent administrator approval before restoring access.
runbook.escalationPath: Administration security on-call -> independent administrator -> incident commander

automatic: Create one high-severity off-hours review item per administrator and window.
Attach bounded AuditLog identifiers and action counts.
manual: Contact the administrator through an independent channel.
Review all affected targets and revert unauthorized changes.

falsePositiveReview.cadence: After every alert and monthly roster review
steps: Reconcile approved incidents, maintenance and timezone-specific roster entries.
Prefer explicit temporary schedules over broad administrator exemptions.

testMethod.procedure: Create one rolled-back synthetic off-hours admin AuditLog row in isolated PostgreSQL and execute the query.
testMethod.expectedSignal: The fixture actor is returned once and a high-severity review item is created.

detection.source: Google Cloud Audit Logs for AlloyDB backup operations
detection.query: resource.type="audited_resource" AND protoPayload.serviceName="alloydb.googleapis.com" AND protoPayload.methodName=~"CreateBackup" AND severity>=ERROR

investigationSteps: Identify the backup target, operation ID and safe error classification.
Check the last successful backup, PITR coverage and recent database or IAM changes.
containmentSteps: Protect the last known-good backup from deletion or overwrite.
Correct the dependency or permission issue and start an approved replacement backup.
runbook.escalationPath: Platform SRE on-call -> database owner -> incident commander when recovery point objectives are threatened

automatic: Open one high-severity incident per failed backup operation.
Attach operation and target identifiers plus last-success age when available.
manual: Confirm coverage of every critical data store.
Run a replacement backup and verify completion without treating it as restore proof.

steps: Identify explicitly cancelled test operations using approved change records.
Review each backup target independently; never suppress repeated failures globally.

testMethod.procedure: Replay a sanitized failed CreateBackup audit entry in an isolated monitoring test project.
testMethod.expectedSignal: One high-severity test incident is created without starting, deleting or modifying a backup.

detection.source: Google Cloud Logging restore-test job logs
detection.signal: Isolated restore verification job emits backup.restore_test_failed

investigationSteps: Identify backup, isolated target, test phase and safe failure classification.
Determine whether integrity, migration, authorization or deletion checks failed after restore.
containmentSteps: Mark the affected backup chain unproven and prevent promotion based on the failed test.
Preserve the isolated restore environment and logs until investigation completes.
runbook.escalationPath: Platform SRE on-call -> database and privacy owners -> incident commander when no proven restore remains

automatic: Open a high-severity incident for each failed restore test run.
Attach backup ID, test-run ID and failed phase without restored data.
manual: Diagnose and repeat the restore in a fresh isolated environment.
Validate RLS, deletion non-reactivation and application integrity before closure.

steps: Separate harness or disposable-environment faults from backup corruption while keeping both visible.
Require a successful fresh rerun before resolving any test-only classification.

testMethod.procedure: Emit one sanitized backup.restore_test_failed fixture from an isolated test job with synthetic backup and run IDs.
testMethod.expectedSignal: One high-severity test incident is created; no claim of a successful restore or drill is made.

detection.source: PostgreSQL AdminAction and AuditLog integrity comparison
detection.query: SELECT aa."id", aa."adminId", aa."action", aa."targetType", aa."targetId" FROM "AdminAction" aa LEFT JOIN "AuditLog" al ON al."actorId" = aa."adminId" AND al."action" = aa."action" AND al."targetType" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM aa."targetType" AND al."targetId" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM aa."targetId" AND ABS(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (al."createdAt" - aa."createdAt"))) <= 5 WHERE aa."createdAt" >= NOW() - INTERVAL '5 minutes' AND al."id" IS NULL
detection.signal: Privileged AdminAction row without its expected AuditLog pair

investigationSteps: Confirm the unmatched AdminAction and inspect transaction, database and logging health.
Check for missing rows across other privileged actions and preserve immutable database evidence.
containmentSteps: Freeze privileged mutations when audit completeness cannot be assured.
Restore the audit write path before replaying or reconciling approved actions.
runbook.escalationPath: Administration security on-call -> database security owner -> incident commander

automatic: Open a critical incident for every unmatched privileged action.
Dedupe by action, actor and target while retaining every unmatched identifier.
manual: Determine transaction regression, tampering or delayed visibility.
Reconcile missing audit evidence under independent review and test the complete pipeline before unfreezing mutations.

steps: Account only for the documented five-second pairing tolerance and transaction boundaries.
Do not suppress unmatched privileged actions; fix query timing or pipeline behavior instead.

testMethod.procedure: Create one rolled-back synthetic AdminAction without an AuditLog pair in isolated PostgreSQL and execute the integrity query.
testMethod.expectedSignal: The unmatched fixture is returned once and one critical test incident is created.
